decision: scaffold first: npm, node>=24 running .ts directly, biome, strict tsc, node --test, ci, renovate
why: every later phase benefits from lint, typecheck and test gates existing before features

decision: ran three parallel architect runners (opus, sonnet, haiku) on the hunk-splitting data model and applier
why: the plan format and out-of-order hunk applier are one-way doors; want structurally distinct candidates before committing

decision: synthesized from opus and sonnet candidates: project file content from base plus applied change lines, no patch application at all
why: all hunks come from one diff so they are disjoint in base coordinates; out-of-order assignment cannot misapply, which deletes the fuzz matcher and its failure modes

decision: temporary index plus commit-tree with fixed dates instead of fast-import
why: same determinism, simpler to debug with ordinary git commands

decision: unanswered review comments are warnings, not validation errors
why: a human must still be able to apply a plan they are happy with

decision: mode-only text files get a TextFile with no hunks
why: the mode unit needs the base bytes to write the file; reusing TextFile keeps one projection path

decision: parseDiff also asserts that projecting every change line reproduces the tip blob
why: catches parser bugs at extract time, before a plan exists

decision: git diff runs with --no-abbrev and --no-textconv in addition to the contract flags
why: raw output abbreviates shas without --no-abbrev; textconv would make hunks disagree with blobs

decision: playback mode narrated by browser speech synthesis, narration text authored by the planner as optional plan fields
why: user wants to watch the branch being written with audio; built-in speech keeps it offline with no key or dependency, and putting narration in the plan keeps one source of truth per commit

decision: tree checks (path-conflict, final-mismatch) run only when the line assignment is complete
why: on a broken assignment they only restate unassigned and duplicate issues

decision: plan base mismatch is reported as malformed at $.base, tip mismatch as stale
why: the stale issue carries only the tip; a base mismatch means the plan was written for another merge-base

decision: two commands over one engine: split for the author (applies a branch, comments feed the next plan) and walk for a reviewer (no apply, playback with narration, comments become a markdown code review)
why: user clarified two personas; the projection, plan and review UI are shared, only the apply step and the feedback renderer differ

decision: commit-tree runs with --no-gpg-sign and messages get a trailing newline
why: commit.gpgSign would make SHAs non-deterministic and prompt for a key

decision: writeBranch returns unchanged when the ref already points at the computed head, even if expectedOld differs
why: the ref is already where apply would put it; refusing would break idempotent re-runs
never rewrites the user's branch unless asked; --name <branch> --force is safe because the final tree equals the checked-out tip

decision: issues and commit lists print 0-based commit indices
why: matches the $.commits[i] JSON paths the planner edits

decision: splitting is per change line, not per file or hunk; a plan takes any subset of a hunk's lines and orders lines of one file across commits freely
why: the user asked that lines move to an earlier commit when the story needs it; the projection engine already makes any line subset well-defined
result: confirmed, limit: no intermediate states absent from base or tip

decision: narration lives in the plan, on commits and on unit refs
why: one planner call produces both the commit order and the voice-over, and the narration stays bound to the exact units it describes
evidence: src/plan.ts parsePlanFile, src/anthropic.ts PLAN_SCHEMA, docs/DESIGN.md Reviewer mode and playback

decision: ran both flows by hand on the fixture: split (plan with a split hunk, check caught planted errors, apply proved the tree hash, v2 answered both comments) and walk (narrated plan, walk server, comment, code review digest)
why: prove it works on the real artifact, not the tests alone; the UI itself could not be opened because no browser is available on this machine
result: VERIFIED except the browser UI, INCONCLUSIVE there
